ravi: Quick report - hit a deterministic-ish panic in the Go sample generator when auth refresh and caller cancel overlap. Repro attached; only happens when sample uses context.Background() and token TTL is very short.

emma: Oof. Paste repro + stack?

ravi: Minimal gist below. This is the exact code shipped in the quickstart sample (so likely copied by users):

```go
// bad_sample.go
ctx := context.Background() // culprit?
c := client.NewClient(ctx, client.Opts{Model: "curie-lite"})
it := c.Generator().Stream("prompt")
for it.Next() {
    fmt.Println(it.Value().Text)
}
if err := it.Err(); err != nil { log.Printf("err=%v", err) }
```

stack snippet: 
```
panic: send on closed channel
goroutine 212 [running]:
github.com/redwood/inference/gen.(*streamer).push(0xc000...)
...
```

ravi: Repro steps: run with TOKEN_TTL=2s and a goroutine that calls c.Close() after ~1s. Run a few times and the iterator sometimes panics, sometimes returns io.ErrClosedPipe, sometimes returns nil but double-closes.

lucas: Two separate root causes I can see: 1) sample uses Background so client lifecycle isn't request-scoped; 2) auth refresh path replaces the transport/token source while streamer goroutines are writing to channels -> races.

lucas: Proposed short-term mitigation: update sample to use the incoming request context (NewClient(req.Context(), ...)) and ensure the iterator has an explicit Close() the handler calls. Also change the sample to recommend singleflight for token refresh.

emma: Long term: we should make the Go SDK protect streams from concurrent transport swaps. Options: a) per-connection token source that is read-only after init; b) use singleflight/mutex to serialize refresh+swap; c) have the iterator hold a reference to a transport that is only replaced once the iterator is quiesced.

ravi: From a DX perspective, users copy the sample. We need both: 1) update quickstart samples now, 2) patch SDK to be defensive.

lucas: API ergonomics note: the current client.Close() semantics are subtle (shuts down shared transport). If we return a dedicated iterator type with Close() error, and document that client.Close() is for global shutdown, I bet this reduces accidental double-close bugs. We can keep current API but add a new Iterator type and a deprecation doc.

emma: Agree. Add an integration test that: spins up an auth mock that forces refresh, starts an iterator, triggers concurrent refresh and caller cancel, runs with -race and assert no panics and deterministic Err values. We'll also add a tiny TTL-toggle script to make the flake reproducible.

parity-bot: PARITY-62: if you change public surface, please open parity ticket and follow checklist.

ravi: Filed INF-4012: "go quickstart: streaming iterator races with auth refresh" with repro, TTL script, and suggested sample patch. cc @emma for the SDK fix PR.

ci-bot: INF-4012 created and linked to nightly -race job.

lucas: Docs follow-up: add a short "Streaming gotchas" section in Go quickstart - show proper ctx usage, iterator.Close ownership, and recommended token-refresh patterns (singleflight, or token-per-connection). Call out the Background anti-pattern explicitly.

emma: I'll implement SDK-side guard (serialize refresh and ensure iterator holds stable transport) and open PR behind feature flag. Will update sample in a separate small PR to avoid blocking parity review.

ravi: Thanks - landing the sample fix quickly will help reduce onboarding friction. Will link INF-4012 when I open the PR. :rocket:
